ledger.x: 1948: the Democratic People's Republic of Korea is proclaimed in the North.
1950: the Korean People's Army invades the South and holds all but a corner around Pusan.
1950: the Inchon landing breaks the North Korean hold on the South.
1950: UN and ROK forces cross the 38th parallel and take Pyongyang.
1950: the Chinese offensives drive the UN forces out of North Korea.
1951: the Chinese and North Korean armies take Seoul a second time.
1951: truce talks begin and the front hardens along what becomes the DMZ.
1953: the Korean Armistice Agreement ends the fighting.
1953: the armistice line gives South Korea a strip in the east.
1953: North Korea gains Kaesong at the armistice.

wars.name: Korean War
wars.outcome: 'Inconclusive'; the Korean Armistice Agreement of 27 July 1953 created the Korean Demilitarized Zone along the front; 'A net total of 3,900 km2 changes hand from North Korea to South Korea', North Korea gaining Kaesong and South Korea Sokcho.

certainty.note: The 38th parallel, the dividing line chosen in 1945, is the southern frontier; the Yalu and Tumen rivers the northern.
The front line moved across the peninsula (June 1950 to March 1951) and then hardened; no positions for 1951-1952 are on the pages opened.
The armistice of 27 July 1953 created a 4-kilometre Demilitarized Zone 'along the frontline'; the Yalu (Amnok) and Tumen rivers 'border China and Russia to the north'.
